items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1803

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to insurance coverage
for out-of-network dialysis


 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Amends Sections 3216, 3221 and 4322 of the Insurance Law.

 PURPOSE AND JUSTIFICATION :
Individuals with kidney failure need regular dialysis treatment, often
several times a week, in order to survive. Although many health
insurance plans allow these patients to travel and receive dialysis
treatment while they are away from home, this coverage is not granted
by all insurance providers. Effectively, this means that some
individuals are faced with the prospect of paying expensive medical
bills for regular dialysis treatments, or staying home. Some
individuals requiring dialysis treatment are unable to travel away
from home for more than a day or two because they cannot afford the
uninsured costs of this treatment. They may be unable to visit family
members or grandchildren, attend weddings, graduations or funerals, or
make ordinary vacation plans. This legislation would allow these
insureds to participate in such important occasions. At the same time,
this legislation would not increase costs for insurers. It provides
that an insurer is only obligated to pay the amount it would pay for
local dialysis treatment, and which it would pay anyway if the insured
stays home. The insured pays not only any regular deductible, but also
any amounts in excess of the local cost of the treatment. The
legislation also provides that the provider may require reasonable
notice of travel plans, as approved by the Superintendent of
Insurance, so that it can make arrangements, if it wishes, with
dialysis providers at the location where the insured intends to
travel.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-2008 - S.2331/A.143 - Remained in Senate Insurance Committee/
Passed Assembly
S.2907/A.2501 - Remained in Senate Insurance Committee/Passed Assembly

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first day of January next succeeding
the date on which it shall have become a law and shall apply to
insurance policies and contracts issued, renewed, modified or altered
on or after such date.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1803A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to insurance coverage
for out-of-network dialysis


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

Provides that insured persons receiving dialysis treatment may go out
of network to receive their treatment.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Amends section 3216, 3221, 4303 and 4332 of the Insurance Law to allow
insured persons to receive dialysis treatment out-of-network provided
that the out-of-network provider is duly licensed; the out-of-network
provider is located outside the service area of the insurer; the in
network provider issues a written order for dialysis treatment stating
that the treatment is necessary; the insured notifies, in writing, at
least thirty days in advance the proposed date or dates of potential
out-of-network services: the insurer shall have the right to
pre-approve the treatment; such coverage is limited to no greater than
ten treatments in a calendar year; and no insurers shall be obligated
to reimburse the out-of-network provider at an amount greater than it
would have paid for the same treatment within the network.

Such coverage of out-of-network services shall also he otherwise
subject to the limitations, exclusions and terms of the policy,
including but not limited to, utilization review, annual deductibles,
copayments and coinsurance consistent with those required for other
similar benefits under the policy.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Individuals with kidney failure need regular dialysis treatment, often
several times a week, in order to survive. Although many health
insurance plans allow these patients to travel and receive dialysis
treatment while they are away from home, this coverage is not granted
by all insurance providers. Effectively, this means that some
individuals are faced with the prospect of paying expensive medical
bills for regular dialysis treatments, or staying home. Some
individuals requiring dialysis treatment are unable to travel away
from home for more than a day or two because they cannot afford the
uninsured costs of this treatment. They may be unable to visit family
members or grandchildren, attend weddings, graduations or funerals, or
make ordinary vacation plans. This legislation would allow these
insured's to participate in such important occasions. At the same
time, this legislation would not increase costs for insurers. It
provides that an insurer is only obligated to pay the amount it would
pay for local dialysis treatment, and which it would pay anyway if the
insured stayed home. The insured pays not only any regular deductible,
but also an amounts in excess of the local cost of treatment. The
legislation also provides that the insurer may require reasonable
notice of travel plans, as approved by the Superintendent of
Insurance, so that it can make arrangements, if it wishes, with
dialysis providers at the locations where the insured intends to
travel.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2007-2008: (S.2331/A.143) Remained in Senate Insurance
Committee/Passed Assembly
2005-2006: (S.2907-A/A.2501-A) Remained in Senate Insurance
Committee/Passed Assembly
 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first day of January next succeeding
the date on which it shall have become a law and shall apply to
insurance policies and contracts issued, renewed, modified or altered
on or after such date.
